steps.text: Hey, you. Yes, you.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: There's no one else here.
I know.
Are you the one who tagged the wall out there, along main street?
You're trying to get away on skateboard?!
Hold up—You've got the wrong idea! I'm not a cop!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: What do you want, then?
I just wanted to ask, do you want to join a graffiti art competition?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Haha, very funny. You expect me to believe the city's encouraging vandalism now?
Here, check this out.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: A pamphlet?
If you're worried about me grabbing you, I'll just leave it over here. You come get it yourself, alright?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: City... street culture... festival? Graffiti contest, skateboard racing, parkour expo, rap battles... and a huge prize pool? And they're gonna broadcast it live?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Did everyone on the city council's brains collectively short-circuit or what?
Don't ask me, they just hired me to do publicity.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Yeah right.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: What kinda hired errand boy chases people down alleys, shouting 'hey, you, yes, you' at them?
Just a habit from my other line of work.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So you are a cop.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Off duty. For now, I'm just passing out flyers for some extra cash.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: If you're interested, take it and sign up. When you register, be sure to get them to write down the number here, and that'll give you access to free mineral water through the whole competition.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And that's how you get your cut?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: ...Listen, girl. You don't like getting questioned? Well, neither do cops, off duty or otherwise.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: If you're not interested, then scram. I don't have time for your little detective game. If I didn't need the money, you can bet I'd be giving you an earful for the vandalism.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (Pats the police officer's shoulder)

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: My bad, I should've known not to pry.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So, I just sign up at this place here, and hand them the flyer?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: (Nods hesitantly)

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Are they still open?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: You're all set, Miss Aciddrop. Do you have any other questions?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Whose idea was it to hold a competition like this anyway?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Representative Cooper of the City Council wants everyone to gain a deeper understanding of our young folks and their street culture.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: At the same time, it's also a way of encouraging the youth to participate in the construction and maintenance of the city.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Gotcha. So it was this Cooper guy's idea, right?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: More or less.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: So is there anything else? If not, you're holding up the line...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Oh, one last thing.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: The guy who gave me the flyer said he'd get paid if I signed up with this number.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: That's right. As long as you show up to the preliminaries tomorrow, we'll send the money to his account the next day. If you make it to the finals or even place, he'll get an even bigger bonus.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Are you also interested in helping promote the competition?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just curious.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: That's fine. You can see here how much we pay.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: ...They're throwing around this kinda money just to sign people up? This Cooper guy must have mad cash.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: (Smiles)

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: That's time! Now, we'll have Mr. Cooper and the judges evaluate the pieces from this group of contestants!

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: The contestants are free to move about the venue until evaluations are finished!

steps.name: Contestant
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: ...Who, me?

steps.name: Contestant
steps.text: Who else? I'm Alba, what's your name?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just call me Aciddrop.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Not from around here, huh? Did you join for kicks while on a business trip or something? ...And why do I get the feeling you're just gonna take home the whole thing?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Hey now, don't sell yourself short. I like what you've done with that, uh...

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Ink.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Yeah, the way you used ink for the whole black and white look is pretty sweet.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: My grandfather was Yanese. He used to dabble in some Yan-style painting, and even taught me a little when I was young. I got bored of it after half a month, though.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: But I went to study under him again for the past three months, just for this competition.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: All that, just for today?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: All that, just for today.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Rad.

steps.name: Security Officer
steps.text: Please stop, you two. You're about to enter the parkour expo area.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: My bad, my bad. Mind if we take a peek? We'll just stand over here.

steps.name: Security Officer
steps.text: As long as you don't trespass into the venue itself, that's fine.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: That the parkour guy over there?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Must be. Looks damn impressive too—

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: A backflip? Is this gymnastics now?!

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: C'mon, dude! You got this!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But... ain't he just a regular old gymnast?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: He's pulling off all these fancy flips and somersaults, but his drops and rolls need some work...

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Is that important?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: 'Course it is.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: He's gonna wreck his knees if he keeps landing like that.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Huh... I still don't quite get it.

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: Contestant Grayson's final time was three minutes and seventeen seconds, a new record for this competition!

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: After retiring from the gymnastics team, Mr. Grayson became the founder of this city's Parkour Association. Let's all put our hands together for his outstanding performance. At the same time, we also welcome all young folks to join the association!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (Whispers) An association? Since when was parkour a career?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Do you think that Grayson guy cheated?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Nah, he won fair and square.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But something about it's just... not cool.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Anyway, let's head back and take a look around.

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: ...Skateboarding contestant... seventh place finish... Skateboarding Association opens every Saturday afternoon...

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: ...Prize... advanced division... breakdance scoring procedure... a more formal competition format, with more rigorous standards...

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: I think I see what you were getting at now, Aciddrop.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: There's something wrong with this whole so-called street culture festival.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: They keep going on and on about these associations—

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: ...Alba...

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: ...Aciddrop...

steps.name: Announcement
steps.text: ...are the contestants who will be moving on to the next round. Please return to the graffiti art competition venue for the explanation of the next round...

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: (Whispers) Representative Cooper, the finalists are here.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: (Clears throat)

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: To all our dear finalists, I am the organizer of this competition, Cooper.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: We put this event together rather hastily, so we would like to apologize in advance for any less-than-satisfactory experiences you may have during the competition.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Hastily? Haven't you been publicizing it for months?

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: About that... Indeed, my inexperience as an organizer seems to have brought many of you a subpar experience, for which I apologize.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: The reason I gathered everyone here is to make an announcement, and express my apologies through my actions—

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: We will hold tomorrow's graffiti art competition on one of City Hall's walls!
This spark an uproar.

steps.name: Impatient Contestant
steps.text: You serious? You're not just messing with us?

steps.name: Showy Contestant
steps.text: You want us to tag the outside of City Hall? You can't take it back, you said it yourself, dude!

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: Please, quiet down, everyone!

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: I put an application in with the City Council through a special high-priority procedure. Please calm down and listen to me!

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: I've had to endure a lot of pressure to make this competition possible. I hope everyone will cherish—

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: (Scans the crowd)

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: I hope everyone will put their most creative ideas on display in the finals tomorrow.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: That is all.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: Next, I will have the staff inform you of the time and place for the start of the competition.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: The outside of City Hall, huh? Cooper's sure getting his money's worth.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: What, is there something special about that?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Not especially, but those pristine white walls are simply begging to be tagged. The cops used to nab people there just about every night.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just begging to be tagged, huh...

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: That look in your eyes... Don't tell me the tagged wall they found you near was actually City Hall?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Eh, what can I say? It really is a nice wall.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: The tug-o-war between cops and graffiti artists around those walls has been going on for over a year. They've had to scrape and repaint it who knows how many times.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Letting people tag those walls is practically a slap in the face to City Hall and the police. I don't know how Cooper managed to persuade them, but it sure smells like conspiracy to me.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Guess we'll find out tomorrow.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: You're going?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: You aren't?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Whatever this Cooper guy has in mind, as long as the finals aren't cancelled, we'll have the legal right to tag whatever we want, however we want, and nobody has any business getting in our way.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I really wanna see what you can do with that ink of yours. I bet it'll be even cooler than what you did today.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Well, when you put it like that, how can I say no?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: I'd better see your magnum opus tomorrow then too.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Who's there?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Miss Aciddrop, I'm one of the staff from the street culture festival.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I'm already in bed. Save it for tomorrow.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: This is extremely important, so could you please open the door?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Thank you very much, Miss.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So what's the deal?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: We've unanimously agreed that you're the strongest contestant in the graffiti art competition...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: No need to butter me up. I know exactly what I'm worth.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: I'll cut to the chase then. Just give me a nod, and we'll make sure you're crowned winner.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just a nod? That easy?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Hear me out first. The champion not only earns more prize money, but also gets to automatically become the first president of the city's Graffiti Art Association—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Perfect, I've been wondering about that. So, what exactly are all these associations, and what are they for?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Naturally, to bring street culture to more people, have more youth participate, and have older folks gain a greater appreciation for it as well.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Take the graffiti art you love so much. After the association is established, it will become a legal government entity, and its members will be protected under the law to freely express their ideas in a reasonable manner.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Even if that expression takes place on someone else's property?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: The association will have a designated venue for its activities.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Okay, say I'm falsely accused of shoplifting by some store, and their surveillance cameras just happened to be down...

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: That has nothing to do with what we're talking about—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: ...I can only spray what was meant for the wall of that shop in that 'designated venue,' right?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Sounds like I hit the nail on the head.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So I can only express my anger 'in a reasonable manner' in that 'clean and tidy' 'designated venue' that even the shop owner would feel dirty stepping in.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Once it is formed, the first legal venue for the association will be the white walls of City Hall. There's no way your hypothetical shopkeeper would miss it.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: ...Is that so?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And will the gentlemen in City Hall allow what's on that wall to go against them?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: There's no need to be so cynical, Miss Aciddrop—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: After seeing your Parkour Association president today, how can I not be?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: ...Is this really the hill you want to die on?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: If you're going to maintain that position, I'd recommend withdrawing from the competition, so as not to make both sides look bad.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Thanks for the tip. I'll keep it in mind.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Well, that left a bad taste in my mouth...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But are they really gonna dedicate an entire wall of City Hall for graffiti?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I won't believe it 'til I see it.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So this is the wall, huh...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Water?
Aciddrop pokes her head out from behind the alley.
She sees that the graffiti she sprayed on the wall last night had gained a few friends, presumably added by people after her.
The policeman from last night, as well as someone she didn't recognize, are pouring water on it.
Splash.
Aciddrop rubs her eyes.
Splash.
Two buckets of cold water in, and everything she'd sprayed had become a cloud of muddy water.

The policeman takes out a colorful rag from another bucket and wipes it along the wall a couple times. The wall's original off-white color quickly reveals itself, with no trace of the graffiti left behind.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: I think there's someone in the alley.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: You and your paranoia. Just hurry up and get the job done before someone sees us.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: What, change of heart? You've been fighting those filthy vandals for over a year, and now you've gone soft for 'em?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: I was just thinking... this new material is amazing.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Apply it to the walls in advance, and no matter what those kids spray, it's gone with just a splash of water and the wipe of a rag.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Of course it's amazing.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: That's what progress is, Officer. Now you'll never have to chase after those little goons ever again.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: And after that association is established, they'll all come here like obedient little lapbeasts and get it out of their system. After all, who in Columbia wouldn't want the backing of the law?

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Then all we'll have to do is check the surveillance footage every day—camera should be coming in tomorrow—and find out who's complaining about what they shouldn't be.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Then I clean it up, and you bring the bastards in to show 'em their place.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: That way, Mr. Cooper can finally put the little troublemakers to use.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: And if anyone starts whining about their lost 'freedom,' we can just say they're giving graffiti culture a bad name and make an example of 'em. Haha! It's absolute genius!

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Plus, the election is right around the corner. This move from Mr. Cooper is sure to garner the youth vote.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: The guy's a genius, I tell you. Keep the brats in line while also earning their loyalty!

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: A genius, huh? Yeah...

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: But what am I supposed to tell them when I bring them to the station?

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Tell who?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: The taggers.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: I used to lecture them about respecting other people's property.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: I'd bring them to the wall they vandalized and make them scrape it clean and paint it over. They'd learn the price of being a public nuisance through hard work and elbow grease.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: But now... how am I supposed to explain that they're being brought in for not doing 'legal graffiti'?

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: Not only that, even if it is 'legal,' there's no guarantee they won't be brought in anyway.

spans.text: Not only that, even if it
'legal,' there's no guarantee they won't be brought in anyway.

steps.name: Police Officer
steps.text: If that happens, what moral ground do I have to stand on?

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: You can stop worrying about shit like that, for starters.

steps.name: Stranger
steps.text: Weren't you dead broke? If you want to change that, then shut up and do what you're told!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Well, that was one helluva show. Good thing I dropped by.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I was hoping to grab some onion rings after the contest, but I don't know a single decent place in this town.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And somehow I doubt I'll find one.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Still, you never know 'til you try.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: There you are, Aciddrop!

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Did someone knock on your door last night?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: I knew it!

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: I was asking around earlier; some people said yes, some people said no.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Did they say why?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: They... all thought it'd be nice to do graffiti legally.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: But I don't want to be told what to do by some association, and I don't want to boss anyone else around either! Who knows what that Cooper guy is up to with these associations—

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Excuse me, but are the two of you Miss Alba and Miss Aciddrop?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: And what if we are?!

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: I'm just here to remind you that the competition is about to start. Please head to your respective preparation areas as soon as possible.

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Hmph. Alright then.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: One last thing, Alba—

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Excuse me, Miss Aciddrop, but we're short on time. Please head to the prep area ASAP.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: (Whispers) So you came after all.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Sure did.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: (Whispers) Can I take that as you having changed your mind?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Well, I must admit, after you left yesterday, I mulled it over and had a change of heart.

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: (Whispers) Excellent, I'm glad to hear that.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: ...The closer we are to the home stretch, the more these finals are heating up!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Let's take a look at this contestant's creative process—hopefully we don't disturb her!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Absolutely astounding! She's using Yanese, uh, ink to create graffiti!

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: (Stifles laughter)

steps.name: Host
steps.text: How refined! It evokes Yan's classical ink figure paintings!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Excuse me, but I see you've written Mr. Cooper's name along with some Yanese characters beneath your work. Can you tell us what it says?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Hmm, how do I put this... It means something to the effect of... eff you.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: It's a classical Yanese swear. Haven't you ever watched any kung fu movies?

steps.name: Staff Worker
steps.text: Cut the camera! Cut the camera!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Now, let's take a look at this contestant—My, oh my! This is stunning!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Those sagacious eyes, those firm lips, that resolute jawline...

steps.name: Host
steps.text: This is, without a doubt, Mr. Cooper! A perfect portrait, no less! It's hard to imagine that this work of art was created by a simple can of spray paint!

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Aciddrop, don't tell me you—

steps.name: Alba
steps.text: Let go of me!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen, as our final contestant finishes their work, we'll soon find out who'll be heading home with our generous prize—and be crowned the King of Graffiti!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: First up is this cheerful young lady's work! Your ratings, please!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Final score, 7.5!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Next up is this, uh... ink thing...

steps.name: Host
steps.text: And to the right are some illegible scribbles... the artist signing her name?

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Final score, 1.0!
Anyone with sharp eyes would have noticed that the Yanese characters Alba wrote are missing.
But amidst the turmoil, even Alba, who was thrown out of the venue and snuck her way back in, did not realize this.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: And next up is this portrait...

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Let us congratulate Miss Aciddrop, who convincingly won the graffiti contest with a perfect 10 points!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Here's your check for becoming the champion. You've earned it.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: And now, you're welcome to give your acceptance speech!

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Miss Aciddrop?

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (Sighs)

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: You gave up one of City Hall's pristine white walls for graffiti, and in the old days, I would've said that's pretty damn cool of you.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But, this so-called contest...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: (Weighs the huge novelty check in her hands)

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: All I can say, folks, is that this is not cool.
Aciddrop suddenly tosses the check high up into the sky.

Then, while everyone is watching the huge sum of money spinning through the air, she grabs the mineral water she'd opened in advance and pours it all over the sagacious, firm, and resolute face on the wall.
Splash.
The face, like her random doodles the night before, turns into a puddle of muddy water.
The staff member in the audience immediately springs up and tries to rush onto the stage, but is tripped by a police officer in the crowd holding a rag and faceplants right into the mud.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Alright, Cooper. You won't have to wait 'til the election is over. Let me show everyone how this brand new coating works—
Before anyone else can react, something comes flying towards the stage from the crowd, and Aciddrop jumps up to catch it firmly in her hands.
It is a tattered rag, stained by all sorts of messy colors.
She takes the rag and wipes it across the wall, suddenly revealing the original off-white color underneath.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just a little water and a rag is enough to make anything on the wall disappear without a trace. A miracle of modern science.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: No lie, throwing a culture festival to bring in the youth vote was a pretty cool idea, Cooper. That is, if you'd really meant it.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Too bad that 'free speech' you were selling was just a fancy whiteboard, and you're more interested in using these 'legal associations' to shut us up.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: This is slander!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: For now you're just playing games with this little wall, but soon you'll have an entire association under your thumb.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And do you really need me to spell out what you, or some Columbian congressman, are gonna do with that?

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: Seize her! She's sabotaging the competition! She's inciting civil unrest! She's a domestic terrorist!
Several security guards step forward stiffly, clearly not expecting any of these dark undercurrents that were brewing beneath the competition.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: If you'd called me a vandal, I might've even felt a little ashamed. Terrorist though? I'm down with it.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But whatever, later y'all.

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: A skateboard?!

steps.name: Representative Cooper
steps.text: Stop her this instant—
The security guards take a few symbolic steps, but in the end, nobody wants to run after something on wheels.
They can only pray that the flight of stairs in front of Aciddrop would scare her off, or at least trip her up.
But the skateboard follows her up into the air as if glued to her feet, and lands on the railing.
She then effortlessly slides down the handrails, makes a sharp turn, and disappears into the dense concrete jungle.
